texts: doha: a moth circling the well like a pilgrim who goes round and round but never drinks
moth, well, empty ritual

Write a doha about a moth that circles the well again and again like a pilgrim performing rounds, never once drinking, a picture of rituals performed with great show but without a drop of real sincerity.
My aunt walked around the village well forty times at dawn for a vow, then screamed at the maid before breakfast, and I thought of a moth going round and round.
Round the well the moth goes, circle on circle, and never tastes the water it came for.
moth, hollow ritual
doha about a moth circling and circling like fake devotion
Round and round the moth performs its rite, and the heart stays far away.
My neighbour does his pilgrimage every year like a moth drawn to the same place, and yet he cheats his tenants all through the rest of it.
Compose a doha about a moth that circles and circles in a fervent dance of devotion, a picture of the person who performs endless rituals with great energy but never changes his heart or his ways.
empty rituals
Many the pilgrimages, many the prayers, and the heart unmoved, like a traveller who never arrives.
My uncle visits a different holy place every year, posts photos of every one, and yet he hasn't spoken to his own brother in a decade.
doha on people who do rituals but don't mean it
Write a doha about the person who performs every ceremony, fasts every fast, and goes on every pilgrimage with perfect form, yet whose heart remains cold, cruel and untouched by any of it.

Please write a doha about a man who turns his prayer beads all morning in front of others, whose mind is far away on money and gossip, showing how outward devotion means nothing without sincerity inside.
doha: guy with prayer beads but his heart isnt in it
prayer beads, fake piety
The beads go round, the lips move, and the heart is a thousand miles away.
My neighbour sits on his porch each evening flicking his prayer beads and watching to see who walks past and notices.
Sandalwood on the brow, fish on the plate at home; he is pure only where people can see.

Compose a doha about a man who marks his forehead with sandalwood paste and preaches purity, but eats fish in secret and breaks every vow, showing that the outer mark means nothing when the heart is false.
sandalwood mark, fish, hypocrisy
Our priest wears sandalwood paste on his forehead every day and lectures on purity, and I saw him buying fish at the stall behind the temple last week.
doha about a guy w sandalwood tilak who secretly eats fish, hypocrite lol

I want a doha about those who go on long pilgrimages and bathe at every holy place, believing it washes away their sins, while they return home and go on lying, cheating and hurting people just as before.
pilgrimage without sincerity
My relative returned from a pilgrimage last week, told everyone he's purified, and by Monday was yelling at his servants again.
Bathed at every holy place, yet the heart is as unwashed as the day he set out.
doha on hypocrite pilgrims
market fish seller, fake saint

Write a doha about a man selling fish in the market who chants loudly and wears holy marks to win customers' trust, but cheats them with false weights, showing how outward piety hides a dishonest heart.
doha about a fish seller at the market acting all holy
The man who sells fish at our market always shouts the Lord's name loudly, then shortchanges every customer who isn't looking.
In the market's din he shouts the name of God over his fish, and weighs his lies with the scales.
The moth goes round and round in its devotion, loud, restless, and singed by its own show.
My aunt's whole morning is chanting at full volume to make sure the neighbours hear, flitting from one ritual to the next like a moth, but she's never at peace.
Compose a doha about a moth that flutters here and there in endless ritual motion, loudly displaying its fervor, but which never settles and never finds the thing that it came looking for.
moth, show of piety
doha pls: moth doing rituals but no sincerity
My grandfather's friend smears sandalwood paste on his forehead every morning, goes to the temple, and then cheats his workers of their pay.

Write a doha about a man who smears sandalwood paste on his forehead and performs every ritual with great care, while treating the poor with contempt, so that all his outward holiness is only a coat of paint.
Fragrant the sandalwood on the brow, and sour the heart beneath it.
doha: sandalwood on forehead but bad heart
sandalwood mark, hypocrisy
The moth is fervent in its circling; the priest is fervent in his chanting; neither one knows what the circling is for.
doha about moth and fake priest
Write a doha comparing a moth that circles mindlessly to a pretender who recites sacred words loudly without knowing or feeling what they mean, both going round and round in empty motion.
moth, empty chanting
My cousin chants at the top of his voice every morning without understanding a single word, bumping around the room like a moth, and calls himself devout.
doha about a guy who circles a tree tying threads but cheats everyone
Round the tree he winds his sacred thread, and round his neighbours he winds his lies.
My uncle goes around the banyan tree seven times every Monday with a thread and a coconut, then spends the week cheating his customers.

Compose a doha about those who circle a tree tying sacred threads and bowing to it, thinking they are earning merit, while their hearts remain full of greed and their dealings with others remain unjust.
tree, sacred thread, hypocrisy
My uncle who owns a fish stall fasts every Monday, chants loudly, and tells everyone how pure he is, then sells yesterday's fish as fresh.
fish, fasting, hypocrite
Fasting from grain, feasting on deceit; he sells his fish and his piety by the same weight.

Compose a doha about a fish seller who fasts, bathes and chants every day to appear holy, yet cheats his customers by selling stale fish as fresh, so that his ritual cleanliness hides a dishonest heart.
doha about a guy who fasts and is super religious but sells bad fish lol
Every week my grandmother walks to the well under the old tree, performs an elaborate ritual, and then complains bitterly about every neighbour.
Under the tree, beside the well, he prays aloud, and the water of his heart is still.

Write a doha about a man who prays aloud by the well under a great tree each day, making sure all can see him, yet whose behavior toward others remains cold and unjust, so his ritual is only a performance.
well, tree, empty ritual
doha: religious show at the well under the tree, but no heart

Compose a doha about a man who lights a lamp at the well every evening, performs every ritual before the neighbours, and goes home to quarrel with his family, proving that outward worship means nothing without a gentle heart.
doha: lamp at a well, all show
lamp, well, show of piety
My neighbour lights a lamp at the village well every dusk so everyone can see how pious he is, then shouts at his wife all night.
Lamp at the well for the world's eyes, and the dark within untouched.
doha about people who go on pilgrimage but stay bad people
Far he travelled to bathe in holy places, and came home as he left, only with dust on his feet.

Write a doha about the man who spends all his savings to visit every holy site and bathe in sacred places, yet returns exactly as selfish and bitter as he left, because the change had to happen inside.
My uncle has done four pilgrimages, but still refuses to forgive his sister for something that happened twenty years ago.
empty pilgrimage
sandalwood, boat, show
Sandalwood on the brow, a boat to the holy place, and a heart that has not left the shore.
My uncle took a boat to a holy site, wearing sandalwood paste and chanting loudly, then argued about the fare the entire way.
Compose a doha about a pilgrim who takes a boat to a faraway holy place with sandalwood on his forehead and loud chanting, hoping to be pure, but who cheats his fellow passengers along the way.
doha: sandalwood and a boat to the holy place, all fake devotion
My brother-in-law makes a big show of fasting for every festival but is cruel to his mother, who has been unwell for months.

Please write a doha about those who fill their days with ceremonies, fasts and elaborate rites while neglecting the living people around them, as if sincerity could be replaced by the number of rituals performed.
Rites without love open nothing, however many are performed.
doha on fake religious people
ritual without love
Write a doha about a man who sets a lamp afloat in a little boat as an offering, ritually exact in everything, but who has never offered a kind word or an honest deed to anyone.
At the festival my uncle floated a lamp in a tiny boat at the river's edge with a loud prayer, and just yesterday refused his own sister a small loan.
lamp, boat, ritual show
doha: lamp on a boat as offering, but the guy is a jerk
He sets the lamp afloat in a little boat, and the dark in his heart sails on.
doha about a potter who does rituals but is dishonest
potter, ritual, show
The potter in our lane does his morning rituals loudly before opening, and then sells cracked pots as perfect ones to travellers.

Write a doha about a potter who performs elaborate ceremonies over his clay before shaping it, bowing and chanting to impress his customers, though he sells cracked work as perfect, showing hollow devotion.
The potter bows before his clay with a show of piety, and sells the cracks beneath his smile.
Compose a doha about a potter who ties a sacred thread to a tree every morning and chants loudly before he starts work, but whose pots are cracked and whose dealings with customers are false.
Thread on the tree and clay on the wheel, and the heart still empty of both.
doha: potter does a ritual at a tree each morning but is a cheat
potter, tree, ritual
The potter next door ties a thread to the old tree before opening his workshop each day, and keeps raising prices on the poor widows who come for pots.
doha: moth in the market at the temple fair, circling everyone, all show
moth, market, show
In the market the moth flutters from stall to stall, devout in every bargain, pure in none.
Write a doha about a moth fluttering through a noisy market crowd with a great show of religious fervor, going from stall to stall loudly chanting, while truly seeking only the next thing to gain.
At the festival market my cousin darted from stall to stall like a moth, chanting loudly at each one, and I know for a fact he cares only about the free sweets.
A fisherman I know fasts every week and goes on pilgrimages, but treats the boys who work his nets like dirt.
fish, pilgrimage, hypocrisy
Compose a doha about a fisherman who goes to holy places and fasts every week, believing it will cleanse him, though he still catches without mercy and cheats the villagers who buy from him.
doha about a fisherman and fake holiness
He bathes in holy waters and returns to the fish, unwashed in the only place that matters.
boat, sandalwood, pretence
My uncle crossed to the pilgrimage island in a boat last year, wearing sandalwood paste, and told everyone on board how holy he was while stealing seats.
A boat to the holy place, sandalwood on the brow, and the same grudge sailing along.
doha: boat n sandalwood, a showy pilgrim
Compose a doha about a pilgrim who crosses in a boat to a faraway holy place with sandalwood on his forehead, certain this will make him pure, though the grudges and greed he carries cross with him.
doha about a boat, a tree, and fake piety
My uncle rowed across the river to the temple tree, tied his thread, and rowed back, then yelled at the boatman who asked to be paid.
Write a doha about a man who takes a boat across to a holy tree, ties his thread with a great show of devotion, and returns by the same boat unchanged, unwilling to treat the boatman with kindness.
boat, tree, empty ritual
Across the water to the tree he sails, and back again, the same as before.
potter, rituals
My brother-in-law, a potter, fasts and prays loudly to be noticed, but he's never once helped his own father in the workshop.
Compose a doha about a potter who performs rituals over his clay with a great show of piety but whose pots are shoddy and whose heart cares only for gain, so that all his ritual is only for display.
doha about the potter who makes a show of praying
He bows to the wheel so that others may see, and the clay is not fooled.
My aunt leaves a lamp burning at the gate all night during every festival so the neighbours can see, yet doesn't give a coin to the beggar by her door.

Write a doha about a woman who lights a lamp and performs her rituals before an audience, hoping to be praised, but who closes her door to the hungry, showing devotion as display instead of sincerity.
doha about lighting a lamp just to show off
The lamp is lit for the neighbours' eyes, and the god within sits in the dark.
lamp, show of piety
My uncle goes to the river each morning to bathe, takes a boat to the holy well across it, and comes back yelling at the family.
By boat to the sacred well, he travels far, and forgets the thirsty neighbour at his own door.
Compose a doha about a man who crosses by boat to a holy well to purify himself, with great ceremony, yet who refuses to give a cup of water to anyone thirsty on his own street.
doha: boat to a sacred well, but no kindness at home
boat, well, ritual
doha about how rituals don't mean anything if you're not sincere
Prayers rise from many lips, and the hearts beneath remain cold.
Compose a doha about those who rush to every ceremony and shout the loudest prayers, hoping others will think them devout, yet who never feel anything genuine and never change a single habit.
empty prayers
My colleague pushes to the front at every religious event, and the next day he is back to gossiping and cheating on his taxes.
My grandmother's neighbour does the water ritual at the well every dawn, loudly, and refuses to give water to the poorer family next door.
He pours the offering at the well and holds back a cup from the thirsty.
Write a doha about a man who draws water from the well for an elaborate morning ritual, chanting loudly for the whole street to hear, who then turns away the thirsty traveller at his door.
doha about well water ritual but no charity
well, ritual, no kindness
prayer beads, show
My uncle clicks his prayer beads loudly through every meeting at the office, and he's the first to blame others when something goes wrong.
Beads for the watching eyes, and a tongue sharp for the absent.

Write a doha about a man who counts prayer beads in front of everyone to look devout, whose mind is scheming and whose tongue is quick to curse, proving that the beads can't clean what the heart hasn't.
doha about prayer beads and being fake
A man in our building does his chanting through a microphone each dawn to prove his devotion, while ignoring the noise complaints of his sick neighbours.
loud show of piety
Compose a doha about a person who makes sure the whole street hears his prayers each morning, claiming devotion, yet who has no patience for the old or the sick living right next door.
He prays aloud so heaven may hear, and the neighbour's trouble goes unheard.
doha on loud prayers vs real kindness
doha: sandalwood tilak guy who's secretly a bad person
Sandalwood on the brow cannot cool the heat of the heart beneath.
The man who sells charms outside the temple wears so much sandalwood paste that you can smell him from the road, and he's cheated half our street.
sandalwood tilak, fraud
Write a doha about a man who covers himself with sandalwood paste, wears holy marks and speaks of virtue to attract admirers, though he steals from the very ones who trust him.
fake prayer beads
doha about prayer beads and not meaning it
My mother-in-law counts her prayer beads through every family argument, and somehow her chant never stops her from taking sides.
Compose a doha about a woman who counts her prayer beads all day yet never forgives a single wrong, who mistakes the motion of the beads for the movement of the heart toward love.
The beads move, the heart sits still, and counting is not worship.
doha: moth in the market chanting loudly, fake saint
moth, market, pretence
A moth in the market, loud in its devotion, selling its fervor for a coin.
Write a doha about a moth fluttering through the noisy market with loud shouts of piety, who sells holy talk to anyone who will listen, though it understands nothing of what it says.
A man at the market stalls flutters from person to person like a moth, offering blessings for money, loudly praising God with one eye on your purse.
My father insists we all attend every ceremony and recite every prayer, but he has never once asked how any of us are feeling.
Please write a doha about the family that never misses a ritual or a fast yet has no tenderness left, where the form is perfect and the love is entirely missing.
doha pls about meaningless rituals
form without feeling
All the ceremonies kept and all the kindness lost: that is a poor kind of prayer.
The potter bows to his wheel in front of the crowd, and the clay beneath his hands is cold.
Compose a doha about a potter who performs great rituals on his wheel to impress, yet is careless in his work and rude to his apprentices, showing that outward show is no substitute for a good heart.
potter, ritual, pretence
doha: potter doing rituals just for show
My cousin, a potter, spends hours on rituals at the start of the day to impress his clients, and then rushes every pot and treats his apprentice terribly.
In the market they sell fish and holy words in the same breath, and weigh both with false scales.
doha about a fish market guy acting holy
fish, market, show

Write a doha about a man who sells fish in the market and loudly recites holy verses to impress customers, yet cheats on his weights, showing how piety on the tongue can coexist with greed in the heart.
At our local market the fishmonger chants a hymn every time a customer approaches, and then charges double for a half-spoiled catch.
need a doha about religious hypocrisy
My boss gave a long speech on honesty at the religious event and then asked me to fix the numbers on Monday.
Write a doha about people who preach virtue loudly, follow all the customs, and look the picture of holiness in public, but behave deceitfully when nobody is looking, living a divided life.
On the outside a saint, on the inside a thief; the face and the heart do not agree.
preaching, not practising
Compose a doha about the pilgrim who walks hundreds of miles to a holy place with great ceremony and returns just as petty as before, because he left the one thing that needed to change at home.
Far he walked to meet the divine, forgetting it had been waiting at home.
pilgrim, unchanged
doha on pilgrimage that leads nowhere
My neighbour has gone on three pilgrimages this year, and each time he comes back and picks the same fight with the same people.
doha: boat ride to holy place + prayer beads, but just for show
My uncle sat in the boat chanting and clicking his prayer beads loudly all the way to the holy site, and then swore at the boatman for being slow.
Beads in the boat, a prayer on the lips, and the heart left behind on the shore.
boat, beads, empty devotion
Write a doha about a pilgrim sailing in a boat to a sacred place, clicking prayer beads and chanting to impress his fellow travellers, while being rude to the boatman who carries him there.
hollow ritual
short doha on fake spirituality plz

Compose a doha about those who shout their prayers, display their fasts and announce their charity but whose hearts remain closed, who treat devotion as a performance and seek only the approval of the crowd.
A thousand rites, and not one tear; the heart has never been there.
A woman on my street broadcasts every fast and donation on social media, and refuses to speak to her mother-in-law.
doha: a fisherman bathing in the holy river to clean his sins but still catching fish for profit
My grandfather's friend bathes in the holy river each dawn and then, still dripping, sets his nets to catch as many fish as he can.
fish, holy bath, hypocrisy
Write a doha about a man who bathes in a sacred river every morning to wash away his sins and then returns to catching fish without mercy, as if the bath had cleaned him of anything but the dust.
The fish live in the holy water all their lives; who then is the purer, the fish or the bather?

Compose a doha about people who make a show of visiting holy places, bathing at sacred spots and giving donations that others can see, believing God can be bought, while their hearts stay as closed as ever.
doha about ppl who do religious things for show
showy devotion
Our neighbour donated a huge amount for the festival, had his name painted on the board, and then turned away the hungry man at his gate.
He bought a name in heaven with the coins of the earth, and heaven was not for sale.

Write a doha about a man who sits at the water's edge in meditation, eyes closed and posture perfect, yet his only thought is the fish he plans to catch and sell, mocking true stillness with his greed.
A man near our lake does a morning sitting ritual for hours, posing for tourists, and I overheard him on the phone arguing about the price of his catch of fish.
Eyes closed in prayer, mind on the fish; the stillness is only skin deep.
doha: guy meditates but all he thinks of is fish
fish, fake meditation
doha about a guy who hugs a tree and prays, but is mean to people
He bows to the tree for the world to see, and turns his back on the one who needs him.
My father touches the old tree and bows every morning on his walk, and hasn't spoken to his own brother since the day the land was divided.
tree, show of devotion
Write a doha about a man who bows to a tree each morning and ties a sacred thread around it for the neighbours to see, but who is harsh to his workers and refuses to forgive his own family.

Compose a doha about a person who lights a lamp every evening with great ceremony and an audience, yet whose heart remains dark with envy and anger, showing that an outward glow is no substitute for inner sincerity.
The lamp is lit and the prayer is read, and the heart stays dark beside them.
lamp, ritual, hypocrisy
My relative puts on a big show of lighting the lamp each evening for guests and then criticises everyone behind their back as soon as they leave.
doha about lighting a lamp for show
Sandalwood cools the brow of the pretender, but nothing can cool the fever of his greed.
The astrologer in our street wears a streak of sandalwood across his forehead and charges old widows fortunes to fix their bad luck.
sandalwood, pretence
doha: sandalwood + fake holy man
Write a doha about a man who paints sandalwood marks on his forehead, quotes the scriptures, and calls himself a saint, while exploiting those who trust him, proving the mark cannot make the man.
A man who runs fishing boats near our town chants hymns and fasts for every festival, yet pays his boat crew almost nothing.
fish, boat, false piety
Compose a doha about a boat owner who fishes for profit all week, refusing to pay his crew fairly, then dresses in white on the holy day and fasts loudly to prove his purity before the village.
He fasts on holy days and feeds on his workers' hunger the rest; the boat and the fish know better.
doha about a fisherman boat owner acting holy but exploiting workers
doha on people who only pretend to be spiritual
I saw a woman post a photo of her donation to charity and then scold the maid for taking a sip of water.
Faith worn only for show is soon outgrown or soiled.
pretend piety
Please write a doha about the difference between truly walking the spiritual path and merely putting on its outward appearance, and how the second deceives only the person doing it.
Write a doha about a fishmonger in the market who closes his stall for a pilgrimage every year and returns glowing with holiness, only to go back to selling old fish as fresh and cheating the poor.
The man selling fish at our market came back from a pilgrimage a week ago and is already shortchanging the same old women who rely on him.
market, fish, fake pilgrim
doha: market fish seller goes on pilgrimage and returns same as before
He walked to the holy place and back to the fish market, unchanged by either road.
